item.description: The short answer: Windows 10 stopped getting free security updates on October 14, 2025. Businesses still running it should upgrade computers that can run Windows 11, replace the ones that can't, and use Microsoft's paid Extended Security Updates only as a short-term bridge. Microsoft ended support for Windows 10 on October 14, 2025. A year later, plenty of small businesses are still running it on at least a few machines. item.description: Updated September 27, 2026 · By Shannon Jones, Roo Tech Services The short answer: Third-party risk is the chance that a vendor, software company or outside service you rely on gets hacked or fails, and takes your business down with it. A good IT provider helps by keeping an inventory of who can access your systems, limiting that access, watching for problems, and making sure you can keep working if a vendor goes down. item.description: Updated September 27, 2026 · By Shannon Jones, Roo Tech Services The short answer: Zero trust is a security approach built on one rule: never trust, always verify. Instead of assuming anyone inside your office or on your network is safe, every person and device has to prove who they are and only gets access to what they need. item.description: Updated September 27, 2026 · By Shannon Jones, Roo Tech Services The short answer: AI hasn't invented new kinds of attacks so much as made old ones faster, cheaper and more convincing. Phishing emails no longer have obvious mistakes, voices and videos can be faked, and attackers can scan for weaknesses at scale. item.title: How to Protect a Small Business From Ransomware
item.description: Updated September 27, 2026 · By Shannon Jones, Roo Tech Services The short answer: Ransomware is malicious software that locks up your files and systems until you pay. Many attackers also steal your data first and threaten to leak it. The best protection is layered: keep systems patched, use endpoint detection and response (EDR), turn on multi-factor authentication, train your team to spot phishing, and keep backups that attackers can't reach and that you've actually tested. item.description: Updated September 27, 2026 · By Shannon Jones, Roo Tech Services The short answer: "End of life" (EOL) or "end of support" means the manufacturer has stopped fixing a product, including security holes. The computer, software or firewall keeps working, but every new vulnerability stays open. item.description: Updated September 27, 2026 · By Shannon Jones, Roo Tech Services The short answer: Defense in depth means protecting your business with several layers of security instead of relying on one tool. item.description: Updated September 27, 2026 · By Shannon Jones, Roo Tech Services The short answer: Co-managed IT is a partnership between your in-house IT person or team and an outside IT provider.
